summary: The item's behaviour at this commit is largely what it says: I drove all five declared falsifications in a scratch copy, proved each landed with a diff, and each reddened the row its falsified_by clause names, so the producer's driven-falsifications.txt is independently corroborated. Two criteria are refuted. AC3 - 'TWO WORKERS NEVER GET ONE TASK' - fails for two ids this contract accepts and the ledger folds into one record: tasks.py validates no id FORMAT (its TASK_ID_PREFIX constant is declared and never used) while claim.py:_safe() maps every character outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] to '_', so 'TASK_0001' and 'TASK/0001' share one claim file. Driven both harmful ways: a live claim on one refuses the OTHER task, and releasing one drops the claim on the other so a second worker is GRANTED a task the first is still holding. AC5 - 'nothing here blocks a landing' and 'never reporting zero as though it had looked' - fails twice: its 'no gate stage loads this' row pins the set of files under .veldo/ and scripts/ that load tasks.py to EMPTY over the live repository, so USING the feature (wiring the read model into .veldo/work.py the way that file already wires frontier.py and claim.py, adding no gate stage) reds the gate; and a task directory holding one set with a single author typo reports 'a .veldo/tasks/ directory that declares no task at all', a false reason and a confident zero. On the central claim I was asked to attack - no second fleet, no pacing - the property is TRUE here (I read the module and checked git: fleet.py is untouched by the item's only commit) but the guard is a nine-name blocklist: a module-level second pool with its own control loop, its own concurrency target and ThreadPoolExecutor workers leaves the whole suite at 61 passed, 0 failed. FINDINGS SHAPE NOTE: the L2 template prescribes severity blocker|major|minor, which .veldo/validate.py rejects (list-shaped findings entries need severity blocking|note), so each entry carries the legal severity plus the template's value in `level`, the convention proof/VELDO-0010/verdict-l2.json also uses.

criteria.note: DROVE THE DECLARED FALSIFICATION. Widened KINDS to a tuple subclass whose __contains__ accepts any string (diff printed, mutation proven landed); the named row reds - 'a task declaring kind BUILD is refused with TASK_KIND_UNKNOWN and the allowed kinds named' - along with the KINDS/CAUSES registration row (59 passed, 2 failed against a 61/0 baseline). Independently re-drove the closed-contract legs on fresh trees: a `waived` key, each of the four missing required fields, a set missing its own id and one id declared by two files are each refused with the cause named and the allowed set printed, while a well-formed set is accepted with zero errors, so the refusals discriminate rather than a validator that refuses everything. I read 'VALIDATED THE WAY EVERY OTHER ARTIFACT HERE IS' as a claim about the validation SHAPE - the same injected parse/fail pair validate.py hands check_requests_dir - which is true; it is not gate-wired, and AC5 says so itself, but the consequence of that is F4. Half of 'the key set is closed' is implemented and asserted by nothing (F8) and the two-files message degenerates when one file declares the id twice (F7); neither refutes the mechanics this criterion is about.

DROVE THE DECLARED FALSIFICATION. Replaced concluded()'s body with `return task.get("status") == "done"` (diff printed): five rows red, including both of AC2's own, its negative control and the two AC4 rows that consume the same read model (56 passed, 5 failed). Independently confirmed both directions on fresh trees: status:done with the product absent reads OPEN and concluded() answers False; status:open with the product on disk reads CONCLUDED and open is empty; the two fixtures differ in exactly one file. produces_problems refuses '/etc/passwd' and '../outside/thing.md', accepts an ordinary in-tree path, and concluded() consults it BEFORE touching the filesystem, so no task can be concluded by pointing outside the tree. One declared-cause mismatch for an EMPTY produces, which the suite's own `or` hides: F5.

The MECHANISM is confirmed and I strengthened it beyond the suite. The declared falsification (claimable() returning every unconcluded task instead of consulting the ledger) reds two named rows (59 passed, 2 failed). Because the suite only claims SEQUENTIALLY, I raced 16 real OS processes at one task id through the real .veldo/claim.py behind a wall-clock barrier: exactly one grant, every other refusal 'claimed'; and 16 processes over 4 distinct ids gave exactly one winner per id, so the per-unit flock really arbitrates and the refusal is arbitration rather than a ledger that refuses everything. Capability and concluded refusals both discriminate against a granting twin. THE CRITERION AS WRITTEN IS REFUTED by F1: two ids the contract accepts with zero errors ('TASK_0001' and 'TASK/0001') are one file to the ledger, and I drove both harms - a task no worker can take, and one task granted to a second worker while the first still holds it, which is the exact outcome this criterion promises never happens.

THE PROPERTY IS TRUE AT THIS COMMIT AND I VERIFIED IT WITHOUT THE SUITE: read all 379 lines of .veldo/tasks.py (no loop construct, no pacing arithmetic, no spawn; desired, resume_at and now are injected callables and only work_remains is the module's own), and `git show --name-only 69f704a` - the only commit that touches .veldo/tasks.py - does not contain .veldo/fleet.py, so 'no change to fleet.py at all' holds by the history and not only by the drive. Drove the declared falsification in its literal spelling (a run_pool method with time.sleep, its own spawn and _organ("governor")): the scan row reds. The loop legs are real and honestly documented - the real veldo_fleet spawns 2 and retires 2 over the real controller, the drain-versus-backoff pair differs in exactly one file (whether the product exists), and the suite records that an earlier assertion was corrected by measurement rather than the loop being bent to it. WEAK GUARD, F2: the absence leg is a nine-name blocklist and a module-level second pool spelled around it leaves the entire suite green, so what is asserted is narrower than what the row claims.

The stand-down legs are confirmed with teeth: deleting the absent-directory branch reds the named row (60 passed, 1 failed); an absent directory and an empty directory stand down with DIFFERENT reasons; check_tasks_dir returns clean over an absent directory; the report carries one key shape either way; and the negative control (a directory present) answers, so the stand-down is a measurement. Two of the criterion's own promises are refuted by driving. (a) 'nothing here blocks a landing' - the AC5 row asserts the set of .veldo/*.py and scripts/*.py files that LOAD tasks.py is EMPTY over the live repository, so wiring this advisory read model into .veldo/work.py the way that file already wires frontier.py and claim.py, with no gate stage added and nothing refused, reds the suite and therefore the gate (F3). (b) 'never reporting zero open tasks as though it had looked and found none' - a directory holding one task set with a single author typo reports 'a .veldo/tasks/ directory that declares no task at all, so there is nothing to divide rather than nothing left', which is false, and no report key carries the set it could not read (F4). Negative-control defect: F6.

findings.text: AC3 REFUTED: two task ids this contract accepts fold into ONE claim record, so two workers can get one task. tasks.py validates no id FORMAT - its TASK_ID_PREFIX = "TASK-" constant is declared and never used - and .veldo/claim.py:_safe() maps every character outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] to '_', so 'TASK_0001' and 'TASK/0001' are two distinct tasks to this module and one file to the ledger. LEG 1: a live claim on TASK_0001 refuses the DIFFERENT task TASK/0001 with 'claimed' and claimable() returns [] - a task nobody can take, which is the spec's own named risk. LEG 2: worker-a holds both, releases only TASK/0001, and the claim on TASK_0001 disappears while worker-a is still working it, so worker-b is GRANTED TASK_0001. This item is where author-written ids first enter the ledger's namespace (construction's are format-checked spec ids), so the gap arrives with it; the fix is one refusal - reject an id whose claim.py:_safe() basename is not the id itself, or enforce the already-declared TASK- prefix.
findings.evidence: probe driving the real .veldo/tasks.py and .veldo/claim.py in a scratch copy: `contract accepts both ids: errs=0`; `ledger basenames: 'TASK_0001' and 'TASK_0001'`; LEG 1 `a claims TASK_0001 -> (True, 'granted')`, `b claims TASK/0001 (a DIFFERENT task) -> (False, 'claimed')`, `claimable to b: []`; LEG 2 `a also claims TASK/0001 -> (True, 'granted')`, `a releases ONLY TASK/0001 -> True`, `is TASK_0001 (still being worked by a) claimed? -> False`, `b claims TASK_0001 -> (True, 'granted')`.

findings.text: AC4's absence leg cannot see a second pool that is spelled differently, and AC4 is this item's central claim. The row asserts 'REFERENCES NO SPAWNER, NO SLEEP AND NO PACING PRIMITIVE', but what it checks is that no AST identifier is one of nine names {sleep, spawn, retire, desired_workers, resume_at_epoch, Popen, fork, Thread, Process} and that neither the governor nor the fleet organ is loaded. Adding all three things the falsified_by clause names - a control loop (`while claimable(...)`), its own pacing decision (a self-computed concurrency target) and a real worker spawner (concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor, with a time.monotonic busy-wait as the interval) - at MODULE level leaves the whole suite green. Nothing asserts the absence of a loop construct at all, and 'ThreadPoolExecutor' is not 'Thread'. The literal spelling does red, so the check is not vacuous; it does not hold the property the criterion calls the shape that must never exist. A closed allow-list (the identifiers this module MAY reference) or a loop/concurrency AST check would.
findings.evidence: scratch mutation AC4-EVADE-module-level, diff proven landed (pool_target() and drain_pool() inserted above class TaskController): `python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 20_veldo_0003_task_source` -> `20_veldo_0003_task_source 35 passed` / `selftest (PARTIAL, 1 of 34 suites): 61 passed, 0 failed`. The same pool written as TaskController METHODS reds only the vars()-derived contract row, not the scan row. Control: mutation AC4-grow-own-loop (time.sleep plus _organ("governor")) reds the scan row, so the row can fail.

findings.text: AC5 pins LIVE repository state to the EMPTY set, so the first real use of this feature reddens the gate. The row's prose says 'NO GATE STAGE LOADS THIS', but the assertion is `_ts_loaders == []` over EVERY file in .veldo/*.py and scripts/*.py, which forbids any consumer at all - including the advisory, non-gate consumers this item exists to serve. Wiring the read model into .veldo/work.py exactly as that file already wires frontier.py (construction's work source) and claim.py, adding no gate stage and refusing nothing, reds the suite and therefore `bash scripts/verify.sh`. That contradicts AC5's own promise that 'nothing here blocks a landing', and it is the shape this repository has been burned by before (a live-state emptiness assertion found in four suites at once, invisible to code review and visible the moment somebody uses the feature). Note that the gate's own first-use stage reports 'no assertion in scripts/suites/ requires this repository's current emptiness' at GREEN while this assertion does, so its families do not cover 'a module that loads this organ'. Fix: assert over the gate's own stages (validate.py's run_all, the verify.sh stage bodies), or assert that no consumer REFUSES anything, rather than that no consumer exists.
findings.evidence: scratch mutation USE-THE-FEATURE, diff proven landed (`TS = _load("veldo_tasks_wk", ".veldo/tasks.py")` plus a task_queue_lines() reader in .veldo/work.py): `SELFTEST FAIL: VELDO-0003 AC5: NO GATE STAGE LOADS THIS ...` / `selftest (PARTIAL, 1 of 34 suites): 60 passed, 1 failed`.

findings.text: A stand-down that reads as a pass over task sets the read model could not read, and the refusals that would have caught them are unreachable. task_report() counts only WELL-FORMED tasks (all_tasks skips unreadable sets and malformed tasks alike) and then, at zero, reports 'a .veldo/tasks/ directory that declares no task at all, so there is nothing to divide rather than nothing left'. Over a directory whose single task set carries one author typo (`targets:` for `target:`) that sentence is false, and it is precisely the 'as though it had looked and found none' failure AC5 forbids. REPORT_KEYS has no key for an unreadable or malformed set and report_lines never mentions one, so read_sets' docstring claim that such a set is 'CARRIED as an error rather than dropped, because a dropped file is a coverage figure quoted without the weakness that produced it' is false of every consumer. Compounded by AC5's own property that nothing in the repository calls check_tasks_dir: the refusals exist as functions no surface invokes, so through the read model a duplicate id lets ONE claim silently cover TWO distinct pieces of work and the second becomes unreachable to every worker - the spec's own 'a task nobody takes'.
findings.evidence: probe over the real read model: typo'd set -> `stood_down=True reason='a .veldo/tasks/ directory that declares no task at all' sets=1 tasks=0 open=0`; unreadable set -> the same reason; one good plus one typo'd -> `task source: 1 task(s) in 2 set(s): 1 open` with no weakness named. Duplicate-id probe: `check_tasks_dir ... errs=1 TASK_DECLARED_TWICE` while the READ MODEL prints `2 task(s) in 2 set(s): 2 open`, then `first claim: (True, 'granted')` and `after ONE claim: open=0 claimed=2`. Wiring: the only reference to the module outside itself and its suite is init_scaffold.py's lay-down list (a name, not a load), while validate.py's run_all calls check_requests() for the peer authored-directory contract and has no tasks equivalent.

findings.text: AC2 declares that 'a task whose produces is empty or absolute is refused with TASK_PRODUCES_UNBOUND', and for the EMPTY case that is false about the code: the one front-matter parser yields None for `produces:` with no value, so task_problems' `if task.get("produces") is not None` guard skips produces_problems entirely and the refusal comes out as TASK_MISSING_FIELD. produces_problems('') is itself correct and unreachable from an authored file. The suite cannot see the difference because its row accepts either cause (`TS.CAUSE_PRODUCES_UNBOUND in out or TS.CAUSE_MISSING_FIELD in out`), an escape hatch inside an assertion about a taxonomy whose stated point is that each cause is 'named separately because each is a different author mistake'. The task is still refused, so nothing is concluded from outside the tree.
findings.evidence: probe: `--- produces empty: parsed value=None errs=1` / `TASK_MISSING_FIELD: task TASK-0001 declares no produces`, against `--- produces absolute: parsed value='/etc/passwd' errs=1` / `TASK_PRODUCES_UNBOUND: ... is absolute, so it could be concluded by a file outside this repository`.

findings.text: AC5's negative control pins a cardinality and controls a different function than the row it names. It asserts `_ts_re_organs(tasks.py) == ["claim", "claim"]`, so adding a THIRD legitimate consult of the same ledger - the ledger's own heartbeat(), which is exactly the 'no second mechanism' behaviour AC3 demands - reds a NEGATIVE CONTROL rather than a behaviour row. A control must add something and assert the detector fires, never pin how many times it fires. Separately, the row it claims to control (`_ts_loaders == []`) uses `_ts_loads_tasks`, a different detector, so the control demonstrates nothing about it; I confirmed `_ts_loads_tasks` is not blind myself by making it fire (F3), which is the control the suite should have carried.
findings.evidence: scratch mutation THIRD-LEDGER-CONSULT (adds heartbeat_task() calling `_organ("claim").heartbeat`): `SELFTEST FAIL: VELDO-0003 AC5 NEGATIVE CONTROL for the row above: the load detector is not blind ...` / `60 passed, 1 failed`.

findings.text: AC1 promises a duplicate id is 'refused with BOTH files named, because "one of them vanished" is not something an author can act on'. When ONE file declares the id twice, check_tasks_dir appends one path per occurrence, so the message names the same file twice - 'task TASK-0001 is declared by 2 files: c.yaml, c.yaml' - which is the unactionable shape the clause exists to prevent, and it miscounts files as occurrences. The suite's only duplicate fixture uses two files, so it never sees this.
findings.evidence: probe: one file declaring TASK-0001 twice -> `TASK_DECLARED_TWICE: task TASK-0001 is declared by 2 files: /tmp/tmptdi9gk7p/.veldo/tasks/c.yaml, /tmp/tmptdi9gk7p/.veldo/tasks/c.yaml`.

findings.text: Half of AC1's 'the key set is closed' is asserted by nothing: deleting the SET-level unrecognised-key refusal from set_problems() outright leaves the suite green. Only the TASK-level unknown key is asserted, and the row that reaches for the set's keys ('a task SET missing its own id is refused too, so the set's keys are as closed as its tasks' keys') tests a MISSING REQUIRED field, which is a different property - so the suite's own sentence claims more than its assertion proves. No fixture ever puts an unrecognised key on a task set.
findings.evidence: clean scratch copy, set-level unknown-key loop deleted from .veldo/tasks.py (`git diff --stat` shows `.veldo/tasks.py | 4 ----` and nothing else): `selftest (PARTIAL, 1 of 34 suites): 61 passed, 0 failed`.

what_i_did.baseline: python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 20_veldo_0003_task_source in an untouched copy of the tree: 61 passed, 0 failed. bash scripts/verify.sh on the same untouched copy: GATE GREEN at dda45bff (4529 passed, 1 pre-existing failure in the spend_recorded mutation slot that the log attributes to the untouched tree).
what_i_did.declared_falsifications_driven: All five, each in a scratch copy with the diff printed to prove the mutation landed and `git checkout -- .` afterwards. AC1 kinds-any-string 59/2, AC2 done-from-status 56/5, AC3 skip-the-ledger 59/2, AC4 grow-own-loop 58/3, AC5 no-standdown 60/1. Each reddened the row its falsified_by clause names, so proof/VELDO-0003/driven-falsifications.txt is independently corroborated for all five. No conclusion here rests on the producer's manifest text.
what_i_did.beyond_the_declared_falsifications: 16 concurrent OS processes racing one task id through the real ledger, and 16 over 4 distinct ids; the feature USED by wiring the read model into .veldo/work.py; a module-level second pool spelled around the blocklist; the same pool as methods; a third ledger consult; malformed, unreadable and duplicate-id task sets driven through the real read model; ledger id folding driven in both harmful directions; the set-level key refusal deleted; git history read to confirm fleet.py is untouched by commit 69f704a; validate.py's run_all read to compare against the peer artifact-directory contract (check_requests).
what_i_did.not_done: I did not review engine/.veldo/tasks.py beyond confirming it is byte-identical to .veldo/tasks.py (diff clean) and did not audit which stage enforces that mirror. I did not run /veldo:init to lay the module into a real adopter tree. I did not attempt a claim-ledger failure under a filesystem without flock.
what_i_did.gate_note_not_a_finding_about_this_item: Writing this verdict file makes the repository gate RED until it is committed, and that is a defect in WARP-0727 AC1 rather than in VELDO-0003. With this file present in an otherwise untouched copy, `bash scripts/verify.sh` goes from GREEN to RED on `WARP-0727 AC1`, whose predicate includes `_v27_domain_paths == _v27_validated` - the git-TRACKED verdict set equal to the on-disk validated set. Measured in that copy: tracked 170, on disk 171, `validated - tracked = ['proof/VELDO-0003/verdict-l2.json']`, `tracked - validated = []`, and verdict_corpus.divergence reports the same file under `untracked`, the key its own docstring calls 'Expected and not red: an author validating before committing is the normal flow'. So the equality leg forbids exactly the flow the corpus owner documents as normal, and every reviewer in this fleet reds the gate by doing what they were asked to do.
